transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Meyers (Redwood AE), Samira Khan (Redwood SE), Aisha Patel (CTO, Terran Labs), Miguel Rojas (Lead ML Eng), Priya Singh (Infosec), Ben Carter (Product)

Summary:
Short discovery for Redwood PLG quickstart and to understand Terran Labs' requirements for hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment. Main asks: time-to-first-token for a proof-of-concept, free credits/quota for evaluation, security posture (SOC2, KMS, VPC), and cost/latency tradeoffs. Agreed next steps include sharing quickstart sandbox creds, SOC2/security docs, pricing for Dedicated/Private, and scheduling a staging benchmark.

Topics:
- Quickstart / free credits / time-to-first-token
- Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem)
- Security: SOC 2, KMS, encryption, audit logs
- Latency vs cost tradeoffs, batching, caching, quantization
- Pilot scope and success criteria

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining uh i'm jordan from redwood, i'm joined by samira our solutions engineer, how's everyone doing?
[00:12] Aisha: good thanks, i got the calendar invite, appreciate y'all making time, we wanted to get a sense for how quickly we can poke at the api and what the hosted experience looks like.
[00:25] Samira: great, that's exactly what this call is for — quickstart, free credits, and we'll walk through time-to-first-token. quick question: are you primarily evaluating hosted first or do you need dedicated/private right away?
[00:39] Aisha: hosted to start, but likely Dedicated later if we hit throughput requirements or need stronger isolation. security is a hard requirement though — SOC2, audit logs, and KMS integration are must-haves.
[00:53] Priya: yeah from infosec perspective we need SSO/SAML, RBAC, KMS, and a copy of your SOC2 report. also data residency might matter for some EU customers.
[01:08] Jordan: totally, we can share SOC2 and our security whitepaper; we also support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations and VPC/private deployment for later stages.
[01:22] Miguel: for the POC, our main metric is 95th percentile latency under a conversational workload — target ~150-200ms per token, and cost per 1k tokens matters. we want to understand batching/caching options.
[01:38] Samira: that aligns. our hosted API can get you started very quickly — most teams get tokens flowing in less than an hour using the quickstart and free credits. for sustained high throughput Dedicated gives predictable capacity and lower unit cost, and Private (VPC/on-prem) covers the regulatory side.
[01:56] Ben: what's the time-to-first-token like — if we drop a small app in and hit the quickstart, how long until we see responses?
[02:07] Samira: if you follow the quickstart, create an API key and run the example, you should see your first token in minutes; realistically from signup to first successful call median is about 20–30 minutes for new users with no infra work. if you want us to provision a sandbox project we can give you creds immediately.
[02:26] Aisha: cool. about free credits — what's included?
[02:30] Jordan: the PLG quickstart includes a credits bundle that covers the first 10k–50k tokens depending on tier; we'll share the exact link and the sandbox credentials. for benchmarking we can extend credits if needed for the POC.
[02:45] Miguel: any gotchas around model variants? we use a mix of Llama-derived and a couple other open models.
[02:52] Samira: we host curated open models and have verified profiles; you can pin model versions and we support automatic fallback to compatible variants. note that quantized variants may change latency and quality, we'll help pick tradeoffs.
[03:07] Priya: if we move to Dedicated, how does network isolation work? do you support VPC peering or PrivateLink?
[03:13] Jordan: Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and can be deployed in a VPC; for Private deployments we offer VPC resident control plane, and on-prem packages for stricter requirements — peering and private connectivity options are available. we'll put the network options in the doc.
[03:31] Aisha: ok. can you run a staging benchmark for our sample workload? we want a 24-hour run to measure cost and p95 latency.
[03:39] Samira: yes we can — if you share a small sample dataset and desired concurrency we'll run a benchmark on hosted and estimate Dedicated cost. SE will own that.
[03:49] Miguel: our dataset is mostly 1–3 turn conversations with average prompt length ~120 tokens, response ~80 tokens. we care most about tail latency during bursts.
[04:02] Samira: makes sense. we have automatic batching and prefix/KV caching and can tune batch sizes and timeouts to meet latency SLOs while reducing cost.
[04:15] Ben: any compliance questions we should know up front? like data retention, logs, ability to turn off usage logging?
[04:22] Priya: also need details on encryption at rest and in transit.
[04:26] Jordan: we'll share the security notebook — covers SOC2, encryption, audit logs, retention settings, and options for customer-managed keys. in Hosted you get configurable data retention and opt-outs for certain telemetry; Dedicated/Private gives more control.
[04:45] Aisha: budget and timeline — we're aiming to get a POC running in the next 2–3 weeks, and a decision by end of next quarter if performance and costs look good.
[04:56] Jordan: timeline seems doable. for a fast POC we recommend hosted quickstart for first two weeks, then flip to Dedicated during the benchmark if you want stable throughput.
[05:09] Miguel: can we request a cost estimate for Dedicated based on our concurrency?
[05:14] Jordan: yes i'll send a sample pricing sheet and we can do a sizing exercise — if you share concurrency and QPS numbers we'll size Reserved capacity and show cost per 1M tokens.
[05:26] Priya: one more — SSO and RBAC, we need SCIM provisioning and SAML.
[05:31] Samira: we support SAML SSO, SCIM for user provisioning and RBAC by role. will include config examples.
[05:40] Ben: any competitors you've seen customers consider?
[05:43] Jordan: commonly OpenAI for hosted, Anthropic, also teams look at cloud-native endpoints like Vertex AI; vector search vendors like Pinecone come up for embeddings pipelines.
[05:55] Aisha: helpful. let's recap next steps.
[06:00] Jordan: recap: samira will share quickstart repo and sandbox creds; i'll send pricing and Dedicated/Private option docs and SOC2/security pack; you'll share sample dataset and desired concurrency; we'll schedule a 1-hour staging benchmark next week.
[06:15] Miguel: yep i'll prepare a small dataset and target SLOs; can we get the sandbox creds today?
[06:20] Samira: i'll follow up in the next couple hours with creds and a quickstart walkthrough link.
[06:26] Priya: i'll review the security docs when you send them and return the questionnaire.
[06:30] Jordan: perfect. thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the items discussed.
[06:35] Aisha: thanks all, appreciate it.
